tasks.objective: Close SEC-2, SEC-3 and ARCH-10 — the three findings that live entirely in `scripts/` — in one task, because they share four files and one of the two scripts sources the other. (a) SEC-2: `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:56` calls `security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s "$LOGIN_KEYCHAIN"`. `-s` is a predicate that takes no operand, so the keychain path is swallowed as a positional keychain argument and the command rewrites the partition list of EVERY signing private key in the login keychain, destroying `teamid:` partitions irreversibly. Bound the selection with `-l "$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME"`, keep the keychain as the trailing positional it already effectively is, and add a guard that refuses to run the command at all when the identity name is empty. v2 note: that guard was UNREACHABLE as v1 specified it, because `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:16` assigns `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing"` unconditionally — no `${VAR:-default}`, no environment override — about forty lines above the call. v2 settles the interface: the name becomes overridable ONLY under `CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN=1`, never in a real build, so the guard is exercisable by the harness without opening a new way for the environment to redirect which CN is created or which label `-l` bounds. (b) SEC-3 + ARCH-10: `scripts/make-app.sh:80` signs with `--force --deep` and nothing else; the shipped artifact was measured at `flags=0x0(none)`, `TeamIdentifier=not set`, `(no entitlements)`, and honours `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`. Replace it with an inside-out signing sequence using `--options runtime --timestamp` and no `--deep`. (c) Build the differential harness both changes need: a sourceable indirection library `scripts/lib/signing-run.sh` that executes nothing at load time, routes every mutating command through one function, and PRINTS argv instead of executing when `CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN=1`; plus `scripts/signing-argv-test.sh` asserting on that argv AND on the indirection's default, wired into `make` and CI. The harness is why these are one task rather than two: split, it would be a hub file between a serialized pair.

SEC-2, the bound selector, differential, and STATIC — the null is obtained by READING the script's source, never by running it. PLAN v2 REPLACES v1's MECHANISM AND KEEPS v1's PROPERTY. v1 pinned a tokenising static parse (join backslash continuations, strip unquoted comments, delete quoted string literals, then tokenise) as the routine six other assertions reuse. Round 1 measured what that costs: the coder disclosed the engine is "plausibly several hundred to low-thousands of lines of bash", the grader's gap 1 recorded criteria 1-5 as failed for want of it, and this task's own budget is `diff_lines: 480` with roughly 235 of them already spent in the round-1 tree (measured against HEAD a0d9b47: 60 changed lines across the four tracked files, 145 in `scripts/signing-argv-test.sh`, 22 in `scripts/lib/signing-run.sh`). A plan that demands an engine no diff under its own cap can carry is a defect in the plan, not in the coder. The engine is RETIRED from this epic and recorded as a deferred finding on the factory side; what replaces it is stated here, once, and every criterion that used to say "criterion 1's pinned parse" now says THE ANCHORED-LINE ROUTINE. THE DIFF CAP IS A LIMIT SOMETHING CAN SAY NO TO: if the assertions this plan version pins cannot be implemented inside the remaining budget, the correct move is `task_status: blocked` quoting the measurement, never a silent overrun and never a criterion left unbuilt without saying so.

THE ANCHORED-LINE ROUTINE — the whole mechanical vocabulary of plan v2, defined here at its only definition site, because a vocabulary that is referenced and never shown is one the implementer reinvents. (1) SELECT: `grep -nE '<anchored ERE>' <file>`, and nothing else. It selects WHOLE PHYSICAL LINES. It does not join continuations, does not strip a trailing comment from inside a line, does not delete quoted strings, and does not classify executable position. (2) COMMENTS NEED NO STRIPPING, because every selector in plan v2 is anchored at `^[[:space:]]*` followed by the command word, and a comment line's first non-blank character is `#`, so it cannot match. (3) NORMALISE a selected line: delete leading and trailing whitespace, collapse each run of spaces and tabs to one space, then append exactly one trailing space. (4) A TOKEN ASSERTION means a fixed-string (`grep -F`) search, in that normalised form, for the token with one space on each side — that is what "the token X is present" and "the token X appears nowhere" MEAN in plan v2, and it needs no tokeniser. (5) SINGLE PHYSICAL LINE IS A REQUIREMENT, not an assumption: every invocation this plan grades must be one physical line, and a graded line ending in a backslash FAILS with `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:N is a continued line: plan v2 grades signing invocations as single physical lines, and a continuation hides tokens from every check in this task` and exit 1. RESIDUAL, stated once and inherited by every criterion that uses this routine: it reads literal text on one physical line, so it cannot see a flag introduced by a parameter expansion, an argument list assembled at run time, or a token hidden after a `#` on a code line. That residual is ACCEPTED by plan v2 on the operator's decision of 2026-09-08, and its price is written down in the deferred finding rather than left implicit. A script that genuinely needs an assembled or indirected signing invocation is a `spec-change-proposed`, not a judgement call.

THE SELECTOR, used by this criterion and by criterion 2: run THE ANCHORED-LINE ROUTINE over `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` with the ERE `^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]+)?security[[:space:]]+set-key-partition-list[[:space:]]`. The optional leading identifier is the indirection function — functional clause 4 requires one, and the unchanged script has none, which is why the selector admits both shapes and why the fixture below is selectable at all. THE INDIRECTION MUST NOT BE NAMED `security` (planner finding P2, carried from v1 with its reason intact): a wrapper by that name makes the anchor ambiguous, since the selector cannot tell the wrapper from the tool. Assert the normalised line does not begin with `security security `; if it does, fail with `the set-key-partition-list line's leading token is "security": plan v2 anchors on the tool name and cannot tell a wrapper named security from the tool` and exit 1. SEC-2, the limit something can say no to. PLAN v2 KEEPS EVERY SAFETY PROPERTY v1 BOUGHT AND REPLACES THE INSTRUMENT. ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS PINNED AND IT IS A SAFETY GATE, not a preference, carried from v1 unchanged: the case runs its STATIC assertions FIRST, and if ANY of them fails it prints that assertion's failure text, exits non-zero, and LAUNCHES NO SUBPROCESS AT ALL. No `bash scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` may ever be spawned from a tree whose guard has not ALREADY been proven, statically, BOTH to be the first executable construct in the file AND to have the canonical refusing form. Placement alone is not refusal, and the state "present, first, and not refusing" is the state in which the launch reaches the creation branch against the operator's real login keychain.

THE CONSTRUCT WALK, REDEFINED AT GREP STRENGTH. THE EFFECTIVE LINES of a file are the lines surviving `grep -nE -v '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)'` — every blank line and every whole-line comment is dropped, and so is the `#!` shebang, which is a comment line. THE GUARD LINE is the first effective line matching `^[[:space:]]*if[[:space:]].*-z[[:space:]]+"?\$\{?SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME`. ASSERT that EVERY effective line ABOVE the guard line matches one of the following anchored patterns — THE WHOLE PERMITTED PREAMBLE, deny-by-default, matched against the NORMALISED form of the line as THE ANCHORED-LINE ROUTINE defines normalisation. (P1) `^set -euo pipefail$`. (P2) the dry-run branch opener: exactly one of `if [ "${CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN:-}" = "1" ]`, the `= 1` spelling, the `-}` spelling, or the `[[ ... ]]` spellings of those, optionally with `; then` appended. (P3) `^then$`, `^else$` or `^fi$`. (P4) an assignment line matching `^SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME=` whose whole normalised text is one of the two texts criterion 4 permits. (P5) `^LOGIN_KEYCHAIN="\$HOME/Library/Keychains/login\.keychain-db"$`. ADDITIONALLY, no permitted preamble line may contain any of the fixed strings `$(`, a backtick, `;;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `>`, `<`, or `source ` — one `grep -F` sweep over the preamble lines, which is what makes "side-effect-free" a mechanical test rather than an adjective, and which is why P2 and P3 are the only compound-statement shapes admitted. NULL, naming EVERY offending line rather than only the first: `ensure-signing-identity guard is not the first executable construct: found "<line text>" at line N before the guard at line M` and exit 1 AND NO SUBPROCESS LAUNCHED. HYPOTHESIS: `ok: the empty-name guard is the first executable construct of scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` and exit 0.

WHY A WHITELIST RATHER THAN A WALKER, and what it costs — stated here because a reader who does not know the trade will "fix" it back. v1's walker classified arbitrary constructs; v2's whitelist admits five line shapes and refuses everything else, so it is STRICTER than the walker on shapes nobody needs and BLINDER than the walker on shapes it cannot see: a trailing `#` comment on a preamble line, a heredoc body, a construct spread across continued lines. Plan v2 answers the blindness by REFUSING those shapes rather than parsing them — a continued line in the preamble matches none of P1-P5 and therefore FAILS the walk, which is the safe direction of failure. The property clause 7(B1) actually needs is delivered: nothing with an effect runs before the guard. The deferred finding records what a real walker would have proved that this does not.

This is where an INVERTED condition dies: `-n` matches no permitted spelling. A BARE `exit` FAILS: after a successful `echo` it exits 0, which is a guard that prints a refusal and then proceeds. (g3) SHAPE — the block contains no `else` and no `elif` effective line. On any failure: `ensure-signing-identity guard is present but cannot refuse: <reason> at line N`, exit 1, AND NO SUBPROCESS LAUNCHED. SEC-2, and this is the criterion that stops criterion 3's test seam from becoming a security hole: the identity name must NOT be environment-overridable in a real build. PLAN v2 REPLACES FOUR CONJUNCTS AND A NORMALISING PARSE WITH TWO ANCHORED LINE ASSERTIONS THAT ARE STRICTLY STRONGER THAN ALL FOUR. Case name unchanged: `override-is-dry-run-only`.

ASSERTION ONE — THE ONLY CODE REFERENCE. Run `grep -n 'CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME' scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` and discard every hit whose line's first non-blank character is `#`, i.e. every whole-line comment: criterion 6 REQUIRES a comment sentence about this variable, so comment hits are expected and must not fail this check. EXACTLY ONE hit must remain, and its NORMALISED text — leading and trailing whitespace deleted, runs of spaces and tabs collapsed to one — must equal CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER the single permitted text `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="${CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME-ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing}"`. There is exactly ONE permitted text and no alternative spelling. The unquoted form is NOT admitted, because the default contains a space and would word-split. The single-quoted form is NOT admitted, because it suppresses the expansion entirely and pins the name to a literal the guard can never see empty. `:-`, `:=`, `=`, `:?`, `?`, `:+` and `+` are NOT admitted, because only `-` lets an explicitly-empty override survive to the guard. And no prefix, suffix or second concatenated word is admitted, because that is precisely the defect round-7 finding F8 found. ONE `grep -Fx` against that one string settles what v1 spent three conjuncts and a normalising parse on, and settles it more tightly: v1's third conjunct enumerated permitted spellings of the OPERATOR and its FOURTH CONJUNCT asserted the complete assignment; whole-assignment equality subsumes both, so functional clause 7(B1)'s reference to criterion 4's fourth conjunct is discharged by this assertion and by nothing else.

ASSERTION TWO — THE REAL PATH IS A BARE LITERAL. The file must contain exactly one line whose normalised text equals `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing"`, and every line matching `^[[:space:]]*SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME=` in the file must be either that line or the permitted dry-run assignment of assertion one. That is what "the non-dry-run assignment is the bare literal with no parameter expansion" means as a check rather than as a sentence, and it is what catches an expansion of the UNPREFIXED name, which assertion one cannot see.

This is the null that catches `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing}"` — an expansion of the unprefixed name, which assertion one never sees because the word `CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME` does not occur in it, and which assertion two catches; the null names either variable for exactly that reason. (2) If the single remaining `CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME` reference does not match the permitted text AND its text contains a colon form of the expansion operator: `CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME expansion at line N uses ":-", which substitutes the default for an explicitly-empty override: the empty-name guard can never fire and case B1 would enter the script body` and exit 1. (3) If MORE THAN ONE non-comment reference remains: `CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME is referenced on N code lines of scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh: this plan permits exactly one, the dry-run assignment, so every other reference is an unguarded override path` and exit 1 — this null is NEW in v2 and replaces v1's reachability conjunct, which asked whether each reference sat inside a `CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN`-conditioned block and needed block tracking to answer. (4) Otherwise, if the one reference does not match the permitted text: `dry-run identity assignment at line N is "<text>", not the single permitted assignment SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="${CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME-ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing}": an override that is not the whole value can make the name non-empty when the override is empty, and the empty-name guard would never fire` and exit 1. All four texts differ from each other and from the pass text. HYPOTHESIS, carried verbatim from v1: `ok: identity name is a literal outside dry-run, and the dry-run assignment is exactly the permitted "-" expansion so an empty override survives to the guard` and exit 0.

THE C-SERIES FIXTURES ARE KEPT BY NAME AND BY COUNT, because functional clause 7(B1) makes "criterion 4 GREEN ... including its C-series fixtures" a prerequisite of the only identity-script subprocess this task launches, and a prerequisite naming a fixture set that no longer exists cannot be discharged. (C1) CONCATENATED SUFFIX — append `-test` inside the closing quote of the dry-run assignment; expected NULL (4) naming that line, exit 1.
